title: Local GPU driver/CUDA troubleshooting breadcrumbs
content:
Quick personal breadcrumbs for the sequence of steps I tried while debugging the laptop / local docker GPU failures. This is messy — notes to self and hypotheses.

Date range: 2024-04-10 -> 2024-06-12
Machine: personal dev laptop (lenovo thinkpad + external eGPU) / local workstation
GPU: RTX 3080 (10GB) — sometimes shows as 10026MiB total in nvidia-smi, sometimes 10240 depending on driver.
Driver + Toolkit situation seen while debugging:
  - Host driver: 535.XX (apt package from graphics-drivers PPA)
  - CUDA toolkit installed in /usr/local/cuda-11.8 and also /usr/local/cuda-12.1 (leftover)
  - Conda envs with cudatoolkit=11.8 and 12.0 tried
  - PyTorch wheel in env: torch==2.1.0 (built for CUDA 11.8)

Symptoms / errors observed (copied raw as I saw them):
  - RuntimeError: CUDA error: driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version
    (seen launching python train_small.py inside container built FROM nvidia/cuda:12.1-base)

  - ImportError: libcuda.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
    (happened in container when nvidia-container-toolkit not configured correctly)

  - CudaRuntimeError: CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version (torch.cuda.init())

  - OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 4.00 GiB (GPU 0; 10.00 GiB total capacity; 6.12 GiB already allocated; 2.00 GiB free; 8.00 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)
    -> This happened even when batch_size=1 on an intentionally tiny model (2-layer mlp), so suspect memory leak or pinned-memory/worker DataLoader issue.

Commands I ran (and outputs I inspected):
  - nvidia-smi -L             # lists GPUs, model ids
  - nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,driver_version,memory.total --format=csv
    -> driver shows 535.54, mem 10192 MiB
  - nvcc --version            # only present when cuda toolkit in PATH
  - python -c "import torch; print(torch.cuda.is_available()); print(torch.version.cuda); print(torch.backends.cudnn.version())"
    -> False / '11.8' / 8400 (varied between runs)

Container repro attempts:
  - docker run --gpus all --rm nvidia/cuda:11.8-runtime-ubuntu22.04 nvidia-smi  # works on host: shows GPUs inside container
  - docker run --gpus all --rm nvidia/cuda:12.1-runtime-ubuntu22.04 python -c "import torch; print(torch.cuda.is_available())"
    -> False (torch build mismatch: wheel expecting 11.8)
  - Verified nvidia-container-runtime and nvidia-container-toolkit installed and daemon restarted.

Host-level investigations:
  - ldd /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/torch/lib/libc10_cuda.so | grep cuda
    -> pointed to /usr/local/cuda-11.8/lib64/libcudart.so.11.0 and also had unresolved references when toolkit 12 present on PATH
  - ls -l /usr/local | grep cuda
    -> cuda -> cuda-12.1 (symlinked) but conda env had 11.8 libs -> classic mismatch.
  - echo $LD_LIBRARY_PATH # sometime empty, sometimes set by .bashrc to /usr/local/cuda/lib64

Memory/OOM-specific debugging I tried:
  - python snippet to monitor memory:
    import torch, time
    for i in range(10):
      x = torch.randn(32, 1024, device='cuda')
      print(i, torch.cuda.memory_allocated()/1024**2, torch.cuda.memory_reserved()/1024**2)
      time.sleep(0.5)
    -> observed memory_reserved increasing even after del x; required torch.cuda.empty_cache(); suspected caching + leak in training loop.

  - Reproduced OOM with DataLoader pin_memory=True + num_workers>0: memory spikes immediately at first batch when num_workers=4. Suspect worker processes allocate pinned buffers.
  - Workaround: set pin_memory=False or num_workers=0. That reduces immediate spike.

Driver / runtime mismatch attempts and notes:
  - Hypothesis A: Host driver (535.x) supports CUDA 12.x, but PyTorch wheel built for CUDA 11.8 — should still work because driver is backwards compatible usually. However, containers and PATH pointing to 12.1 toolkit cause ldconfig/ldd to pick wrong libcuda at runtime -> mismatch error.
  - Hypothesis B: There are leftover files from system CUDA installs in /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu that shadow conda libs.
  - Hypothesis C: nvidia-container-toolkit not mounting libcuda in some container variants, resulting in 'libcuda.so.1 missing' inside container. Verified with 'docker run --rm --gpus all nvidia/cuda:12.1-base ls -l /usr/local/nvidia/lib64 | head'

What I tried to fix (and result):
  - Reinstalled NVIDIA driver (apt purge -> add-apt-repository ppa:graphics-drivers -> apt install nvidia-driver-535)
    -> After reboot, host nvidia-smi ok. Did not fix container torch import errors.
  - Remove /usr/local/cuda-12.1 symlink, point /usr/local/cuda -> cuda-11.8 (temporary)
    -> python in host env now shows torch.cuda.is_available() = True in some envs. But containers built from 12.1 base still fail.
  - Rebuilt local docker image FROM nvidia/cuda:11.8-runtime, installed pip wheel for torch 2.1 (CUDA 11.8) -> fixed torch.cuda.is_available() inside container.
  - For the OOM case: set DataLoader(pin_memory=False), num_workers=0 -> run succeeded under low batch size.

Logs / dmesg extracts I kept:
  - Apr 12 10:13:44 laptop kernel: [12345.678901] Out of memory: Killed process 3261 (python) total-vm:123456kB, anon-rss:987654kB, file-rss:0kB, shmem-rss:0kB
  - Apr 12 10:13:44 laptop kernel: [12345.679012] python invoked oom-killer: gfp-mask=0x20d2ca, order=0, oom_score_adj=0
  -> This indicates severe host memory pressure (not necessarily GPU-only). Need to check swap usage and system memory pressure when dataloader workers spawn pinned buffers.

Open questions / TODO (prioritized):
  1) Investigate whether DataLoader pinned-memory allocation is leaking on this kernel/driver combo. Steps: reproduce with small script that spawns workers and repeatedly creates pin_memory tensors. Collect /proc/<pid>/smaps and /proc/<pid>/status to see locked memory.
  2) Add test that runs inside nvidia/cuda:11.8 vs 12.1 images to reproduce lib mismatch -> create minimal Dockerfile and upload to GH issue.
  3) Try switching to conda-installed cudatoolkit=11.8 (instead of system /usr/local/cuda) and ensure LD_LIBRARY_PATH empty to force conda libs used. Document steps that reliably fixed it for me.
  4) Check with SRE/infra if graphics-driver PPA upgrade is allowed on workstation fleet: we may need driver pinned across dev fleet.

Workaround notes (what I keep using locally):
  - For containers: base images must match PyTorch wheel CUDA version (11.8 wheels -> use nvidia/cuda:11.8-runtime).
  - For quick tests: conda create -n torch11 python=3.10 pytorch==2.1 torchvision cudatoolkit=11.8 -c pytorch -c conda-forge -> seems consistent.
  - For OOM: set pin_memory=False on DataLoader and reduce num_workers to 0 if on laptop. On CI / Dedicated machines with large RAM, pin_memory can be enabled.

Notes to self (less formal):
  - Keep docker images labelled clearly with CUDA version in README -> stops confusion.
  - When hitting driver/runtime mismatch -> always check ldd on the torch cuda libs and nvidia-smi inside container.
  - If you see 'driver version is insufficient', try reboot after driver reinstall (old driver still loaded).
  - If libcuda missing in container: ensure --gpus all passed and nvidia-container-toolkit installed.

Snippets to paste into issues / troubleshooting template: (copy-paste friendly)
  - nvidia-smi output:
    +---------------------------------+
    | NVIDIA-SMI 535.54       Driver Version: 535.54       CUDA Version: 12.1 |
    +---------------------------------+
  - Python checks:
    python -c "import torch; print(torch.__version__); print(torch.version.cuda); print(torch.cuda.is_available())"

  - Quick repro script for DataLoader spike:
    import torch, time
    from torch.utils.data import DataLoader, Dataset

    class Dummy(Dataset):
        def __len__(self): return 100000
        def __getitem__(self, i): return torch.randn(1024), 0
\    loader = DataLoader(Dummy(), batch_size=1, num_workers=4, pin_memory=True)
    for i, (x,y) in enumerate(loader):
        if i%10==0:
            print(i, torch.cuda.memory_reserved(0)/1024**2, torch.cuda.memory_allocated(0)/1024**2)
        if i>100: break

    -> observe large jump on first worker spawn.

Final short summary:
  - Primary root causes seen: mismatched container base CUDA vs PyTorch wheel; host /usr/local/cuda symlink pointing to different toolkit; DataLoader pinned memory causing host RAM pressure and apparent OOMs.
  - Short-term fixes: align container CUDA version to wheel, use conda cudatoolkit for dev envs, disable pin_memory / reduce num_workers on laptop.

If I make this reproducible I'll attach a minimal Dockerfile + script and open GH issue (INF-312)

-- Ava
